scope: Per-session source-runtime Linux child-subreaper/pidfd cleanup after EOF/SIGTERM and Studio owner SIGKILL. macOS ordinary group cleanup remains compatible. No VM, desktop app, installer or DMG changed.

reproduced_before_fix.observed: daemon survived owner shutdown outside the SDK group
reproduced_before_fix.proof: Actual tool execution on the pre-fix image. The test killed only its own remaining fixture process during cleanup; no baseline XML was retained.

implementation: Each supported Linux stdio launch now owns a separate stdlib-only supervisor process. Both one-shot and persistent sessions use the same parameter construction; existing selected environment and permission logic are retained.

The supervisor becomes a child subreaper, forwards unchanged raw input with bounded buffering and monitors owner HUP even under backpressure. Cleanup reads only its own direct/adopted child view, opens stable pidfds, verifies parentage, kills and reaps within one second.

Already-closed input is rejected before server launch. Initialization and cleanup errors remain redacted on stderr; no unwrapped server retry is added. Unsupported platforms keep SDK behavior; unavailable Linux kernel support logs the limitation.

Prepared fixed internal frozen-worker dispatch and raw worker-file inclusion, with portable unit proof only. No frozen Linux binary or app was built. The existing example now supports a guarded --detached mode.

linux.report_kind: Captured completion output from the actual Docker exec tool, including four escaped-daemon case receipts and the final pytest count. The initial 32 progress dots were a previous output chunk.

verified: Real Linux SDK sessions stop a double-forked SIGTERM-resistant daemon that changed process group, on normal Studio close and owner SIGKILL, in both one-shot and persistent modes. The outer test process stays alive, so container exit cannot manufacture cleanup.

Kernel pidfd exit checks confirm server and escaped daemon stop. An unrelated sentinel remains alive. Exactly one invocation is recorded and no work is replayed. Actual close/kill case settlement is about 0.008-0.012 seconds on this fixture.
Both thin-example modes stop detached children. Already-closed owner input never launches a server; EOF still stops a server that filled both relay and child stdin buffers.

Portable guards verify source/frozen argument handling, original selected environment outside argv, explicit unsupported-Linux warning, checked parentage, pidfd signalling, unavailable cleanup and redacted diagnostics.
Host MCP connection, remote HTTP, SDK bridge, worker dispatch and packaging regressions pass. Existing macOS one-shot/persistent resistant-process-group shutdown passes separately.
All temporary acceptance containers are removed. No raw Docker socket, host data, published port, credentials or external account is used inside the Linux runtime.

fixture.runtime: uid/gid 65534, network none, read-only root, capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, pids128/memory768MiB/cpu2 and bounded tmpfs. No host mounts or daemon socket.
fixture.test_tmpfs: The final trusted test tmpfs explicitly allows exec so packaging unit fixtures can satisfy os.access(X_OK). Initial default-noexec runs correctly failed three packaging assertions; a separate probe confirmed X_OK false despite mode0755. Production analysis filesystem restrictions are unchanged.
fixture.report_retention: JUnit written into tmpfs vanished when the container stopped; retained actual completion-tool output instead. No missing XML is represented as an existing file.

compatibility.upgrade: Stop active MCP calls, update the source package and restart normally. Supported Linux sessions gain supervision automatically; no configuration or data migration. Existing installers do not contain this source change.
compatibility.rollback: Prior versions retain SDK group cleanup and its detached-child limitation. No persisted state needs rollback.
compatibility.cost: One small isolated Python supervisor process per active stdio session. Persistent pooling retains its existing session sharing/limits.

pending: Actual personal VM deployment, host bind/UID checks, authenticated HTTPS, upgrade/full restore, daemon restart and power-loss remain separate.

Direct SIGKILL of the supervisor, hostile executables, changed privileges/namespaces, oversized fork trees beyond the bounded cleanup budget and host root need a service cgroup/container boundary. This is cleanup ownership, not a security sandbox.
Detached host processes on macOS/Windows and Linux without kernel/procfs support remain outside the new acceptance. Existing ordinary macOS SDK groups are verified only.
Frozen Linux execution, installed/native OS releases, other SDK/kernel versions, physical devices and selected external accounts remain separate.

quality.ruff: All nine changed/new supervisor, bridge, example and fixture/test modules pass without rule exclusions.
